title: Regular expressions basics
summary: Describe text patterns with regular expressions to test, find and replace text.

docs.title: MDN: Regular expression syntax cheat sheet

quiz.explain: `^` and `$` mark the start and end, and `\d{3}` means exactly three digits. `'456'` fits.
`\d+` matches one or more digits in a row, and the `g` flag finds every such run: `1`, `22` and `333`.
`?` makes the letter before it optional, so the `u` may be present or absent.

quiz.q: Complete the pattern so it matches one or more whitespace characters.
quiz.explain: `\s` is any whitespace character and `+` means one or more, so any run of spaces collapses into one.

options: Makes the pattern ignore upper and lower case
Finds all matches instead of stopping at the first
Turns the pattern into a string
quiz.explain: `g` means global. Without it, `match` and `replace` handle only the first match. The case-insensitive flag is `i`.

exercise.task:
In `regex.js`, write four functions using regular expressions:

- `isPhone(text)` is `true` only for exactly 10 digits and nothing else, such as `'9876543210'`.
- `findNumbers(text)` returns an array of all numbers in the text, as numbers: `'a1b22'` gives `[1, 22]`. Return `[]` if there are none.
- `isCollegeEmail(text)` is `true` when the text looks like `name@college.edu`: one or more letters, digits, dots or underscores before the `@`, and it ends with `@college.edu`.
- `cleanSpaces(text)` replaces every run of whitespace with one space and removes spaces at the ends.
hints: Write a pattern between slashes, like `/^\d{10}$/`, and test text with `pattern.test(text)`. The `^` and `$` anchors force the whole text to match.
`text.match(/\d+/g)` returns an array of strings or `null` when nothing matches, so use `?? []` and then `.map(Number)`. For spaces use `text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()`.
